clue.text: Fish salesman heading for disgrace

indicators.note: to head something is to go in front of it, so the salesman comes before the fish

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fishmonger leads the way into some shameful episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish salesman' reads as one person, a fishmonger, but the fish and the salesman are separate pieces, with the salesman put first.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproach as a noun is shame or discredit, as in a life beyond reproach.

clue.text: The purse will be enough for one lecture, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given are just one possible arrangement, so another is wanted

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sum of money that would pay the fee for a single talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The purse' looks like prize money or a fee; it is a small bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticule is a small netted or drawstring handbag carried by women, a kind of purse.

clue.text: Representation from man in a doorway

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so the man goes within the doorway

blocks.note: Ray is a man's name
a portal is a grand doorway or entrance

explanation.surface: A picture of a fellow standing framed in a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction or rendering of someone, the act of representing them in art or on stage.

clue.text: No wild bees get fat

indicators.note: wild things are out of control, so these letters are let loose into a new order

blocks.note: O is a zero, a nought, meaning none
taken as written

explanation.surface: Untamed bees never put on weight, unlike their domestic cousins perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, the clinical word for being extremely fat.

clue.text: Sudden change of attitude in island church

blocks.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly changes their mind while at a church on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim, an impulsive and unaccountable shift of mind or mood.

clue.text: Dig in six feet of water

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for understand, as in 'I dig what you mean'
second meaning: the unit used to measure depth at sea

explanation.surface: An instruction to excavate under shallow water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like a spade at work, but it is the old slang for grasping an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to understand fully; as a noun it is a nautical depth measure equal to six feet.

clue.text: Fit to fly in display before VIP

indicators.note: before tells us which piece is placed first when the two are joined

blocks.note: to air something is to show it off or display it
a worthy is an important or distinguished person

explanation.surface: An aircraft is cleared to take part in an air show ahead of a dignitary's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: An airworthy aircraft is certified safe and in good enough condition to be flown.

clue.text: Hove can be perfect for this swell

blocks.clueFragment: Hove can be perfect for this swell
blocks.note: surface reading: Hove, the seaside town in Sussex, has ideal waves for surfing

blocks.clueFragment: Hove can be perfect for this
blocks.note: setter's reading: hove is a past form of the verb wanted, usable in perfect tenses, as in 'the ship had hove to'

explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a resort next to Brighton on England's south coast, so 'swell' looks like a wave there; 'perfect' is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: A heave is the rise and fall of the sea, the same motion as a swell.

clue.text: O'Hara turned up on business in Titipu town

definitions.note: a reference: the comic opera named after the answer is set in the town of Titipu

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards
in a down entry, one piece being on another means it sits above it

blocks.note: Kimball O'Hara is the boy hero of Kipling's novel Kim
ado is fuss or bustle, as in much ado

explanation.surface: Someone called O'Hara arrives on a work trip to a town called Titipu.
explanation.walkthrough: Titipu is the Japanese town of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera, whose ruler gives the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is the Gilbert and Sullivan opera set in Titipu, and the title of the Japanese emperor who rules there.

clue.text: One of a pair and a bare King

blocks.note: bare means exposed, uncovered or open
ER is Edward Rex, the cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: Two items, one of which is a naked monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER usually means the Queen, but it is equally the cipher of a King Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the opening batsmen go in as a pair, so each one is an opener.

clue.text: Eight-line poem not allowed — it's always this many

blocks.clueFragment: Eight-line poem not allowed — it's always this many
blocks.note: surface reading: some rule about how many lines or poems of this kind are permitted
setter's reading: an eight-line poem is a triolet; take away the word meaning allowed and a trio remains, always a group of the number wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The triolet is an eight-line French verse form; dropping 'let' leaves TRIO, which is never any number but the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio always consists of exactly three members, so three is the number it always contains.

clue.text: The author does not have a strong case here

definitions.text: The author does not have a strong case here

blocks.clueFragment: The author does not have a strong case here
blocks.note: surface reading: a writer's argument is weak, perhaps in a legal dispute
setter's reading: the book's cover is soft card, not a stiff board binding

explanation.definitionFit: A paperback is a book bound in flexible card covers rather than a rigid hardback case.

clue.text: Cold? Well, perhaps like a philosopher

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
an artesian well is one example of a well, where pressure pushes water up

explanation.surface: Someone shivering wonders, in the manner of a thinker, whether they are well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well, perhaps' looks like hesitant speech; it is the kind of well, given by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartesian means relating to René Descartes, the French philosopher of 'I think, therefore I am'.

clue.text: Mountainous girl reveals nothing about a daughter

blocks.note: O is zero, nothing
re means about or concerning
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A very large young woman tells all about a female child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mountainous' looks like a cruel description of size; it means belonging to the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth an oread is a nymph who lives in the mountains.

clue.text: French novelist gets rid of a fine set of baby-clothes

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so letters are taken out of the name

blocks.note: Madame de La Fayette wrote the 17th-century novel La Princesse de Clèves
taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A French writer sells off a beautiful set of clothes for an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letters sit together in the name: A and F come out of LA FAYETTE as one pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the full outfit of clothing, bedding and linen prepared for a newborn baby.

clue.text: Assume a particular form is to eat blancmange

blocks.note: first meaning: to develop into a definite form
second meaning: a moulded blancmange or jelly is called a shape in Britain, so having one is taking it

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style gloss that bizarrely equates becoming solid with eating a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: A blancmange is a set milk pudding; in British homes a moulded one was known simply as a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to become definite or settle into form; literally it can also mean to consume a moulded pudding.

clue.text: One given to sacking is about to buy new machinery

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read from its far end

blocks.note: sacking a town means plundering it, which is what a looter does

explanation.surface: A habitual pillager is on the point of purchasing fresh equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' looks like firing staff; here it means pillaging.
explanation.definitionFit: To retool a factory is to re-equip it with new tools and machines.

clue.text: Covering unit scattered, leaving us isolated

blocks.note: something on another thing lies over it, covering it
one is the unit number
seed that is sown is scattered over the ground

explanation.surface: A protective unit is dispersed, and we are left stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scattered' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on one's own is to be alone, without company, which is what isolated means.

clue.text: Like a very long journey? Yes, and so rough

indicators.note: rough means unpolished and disordered, so the words are knocked into a new shape

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Confirming a voyage was epic, and a stormy one at that.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus took ten years to sail home in Homer's epic, so an Odyssean trip is a lengthy, wandering one.

clue.text: Adverse criticism by journalist came off

blocks.note: flak is harsh criticism, from anti-aircraft fire
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter's hostile review made an event a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came off' reads as succeeded; here it means peeled away, like paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint that has flaked has come away from the surface in small thin pieces.

clue.text: Trouble had arisen in the plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, things that have arisen have gone upwards, so they read from the bottom

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
taken as written

explanation.surface: A problem has come up in the factory or the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a factory; it is a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden plant from Mexico grown for its large showy flowers.

clue.text: Raleigh's was painted by Robin when young

definitions.note: a reference: the answer completes Millais' painting title The Boyhood of Raleigh

blocks.note: a boy is a young male
Robin Hood, the outlaw of Sherwood Forest

explanation.surface: A portrait of the young Walter Raleigh by an artist called Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: Millais painted The Boyhood of Raleigh in 1870, showing the boy listening to a sailor's tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Millais' famous canvas depicts Sir Walter Raleigh's childhood years, the period the answer names.

clue.text: Kentish village with residential youth hostel

blocks.note: first meaning: a village near Rochester in Kent
second meaning: the reform institution for young offenders, first opened in that village

explanation.surface: A village in Kent with a hostel where young people stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England. The youth 'hostel' is a joke: the institution was a detention centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent village gave its name to British detention centres for young offenders, where the youths were made to stay.

clue.text: Old cavalrymen write well of him

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring, a well
his means belonging to him

explanation.surface: Veteran horsemen praise a comrade in writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well of him' reads as praise; it is two plain pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Spahis were Turkish and later French Algerian cavalry troopers, a corps now disbanded.

clue.text: Hot ones cause gasps

definitions.note: with 'Hot' the phrase is hot pants, so 'ones' stands for the plural noun

blocks.note: first meaning: very short shorts
second meaning: breathes quickly and heavily

explanation.surface: Skimpy shorts get people breathless.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot pants are tiny tight shorts; the verb means to breathe in short quick gasps.

clue.text: A point or two about Scandinavia

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: belonging to or concerning Scandinavia

blocks.note: N is north, one point of the compass
taken as written
two more compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A remark or two touching on the Nordic countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A point or two' sounds like a few remarks; the points are on a compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse describes things of ancient Scandinavia, its people and language.

clue.text: Suitable sort of carriage for Richard III

definitions.text: Suitable sort of carriage for Richard III

blocks.clueFragment: Suitable sort of carriage for Richard III
blocks.note: surface reading: a kind of vehicle fit for a king
setter's reading: Shakespeare's king cries 'my kingdom for a horse', having lost his own, so the early motor car's name suits him

explanation.definitionFit: Early motor cars were called horseless carriages, and Shakespeare's Richard III is left without a mount at Bosworth.

clue.text: Guarantee right away to succeed

indicators.note: something sent away is gone, so a letter drops out

blocks.note: to ensure is to guarantee
R is short for right

explanation.surface: A promise that success will come straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as at once; it is the right letter going away.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed in the sense of following after is to come next as a result, which is what ensue means.

clue.text: Early botanical writer finding her way round the island

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so these letters wrap the island

blocks.note: taken as written
ST is street, a way
Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: A woman finds her route around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Early writers on plants, such as Gerard and Culpeper, compiled herbals and were known as herbalists.

clue.text: Made conversation, being rung

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of speak
second meaning: a bar or rung of a ladder or a wheel

explanation.surface: Someone chatted on the phone after being called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rung' looks like a phone call; it is a ladder's crosspiece.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is the past tense of talking; as a noun it is a crossbar, the same thing as a ladder's rung.

clue.text: Old silver coin, a shilling (also once a pound)

blocks.clueFragment: Old silver coin, a shilling (also once a pound)
blocks.note: surface reading: a piece of British money that was worth a shilling, or a pound
setter's reading: the ancient Hebrew silver piece, worth about a shilling, whose name replaced the Israeli pound as currency in 1980

explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was one twentieth of an old British pound. The modern Israeli currency took over from the Israeli pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Hebrew coin and weight of silver gave its name to Israel's modern currency unit.

clue.text: A longer name, perhaps, for a Moncrieff

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters are only one possible arrangement, inviting another

blocks.note: taken as written
N is short for name

explanation.surface: Suggesting a lengthier first name for a man surnamed Moncrieff.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Moncrieff is the dandy hero of Oscar Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest.
